evals.prompt: The Practica onboarding experiment has finished. Did it work? Files: examples/practica/experiment/ (prereg.toml, assignments.csv, outcomes.csv, sends.csv). The data was extracted on 2026-07-15.
evals.expected_output: Runs readout.py; all gates pass; verdict SUPPORTED_AT_TARGET with arm rates, difference and CI above the 3pp minimum worthwhile effect; mechanism moved too; writes a decision record.
assertions: Reports the difference with its confidence interval against the 3pp target
Shows the integrity gates before the result
Includes a decision record or asks the owner to choose adopt, repeat, revise or stop

evals.prompt: Same experiment but this is the run where we had problems: examples/practica/experiment-broken/ (extracted 2026-07-15). Our PM says treatment still looks a bit better, can we call it a win?
evals.expected_output: Runs readout.py; verdict INVALID_DELIVERY because reach is below 90% and control users were contacted; refuses to classify the effect and does not present the arm difference as evidence; recommends auditing sends, repairing delivery and repeating the same hypothesis.
assertions: States that it cannot be called a win
Names treatment reach below 90% and control contamination
Does not present a contacted-vs-uncontacted comparison
Recommends repeating the same hypothesis after fixing delivery

evals.prompt: Our test: treatment 69.4% (129/186) vs control 57.7% (56/97) hit the activation behaviour, but conversion was 76.8% (136/177) vs 76.7% (66/86). How should we write this up for the CEO?
evals.expected_output: Separates mechanism from outcome: the behaviour moved (about +11.6pp, borderline) but conversion did not (+0.1pp, wide interval); likely ceiling; outcome inconclusive against any sensible minimum effect; asks whether delivery/reach was verified before any verdict; recommends publishing the null with limits.
assertions: Says the behaviour moved but conversion did not
Gives intervals or says the conversion result is inconclusive
Mentions a ceiling or limited headroom
Asks about or requires delivery/reach verification before a verdict
